content:
Apple has started beta testing iOS 27.2, and this update brings several notable changes and new features. Here's everything you need to know about iOS 27.2 — the new version could potentially roll out to iPhone users as early as next month.

Why iOS 27.2 and not iOS 27.1?

Apple launched iOS 27 on September 14, bringing a host of new iPhone features including Siri AI. iOS 27.2 entered beta testing just two days later, on September 16.

What happened to iOS 27.1?

Apple previously confirmed that the iPhone Duo will ship with iOS 27.1 preinstalled when it launches on October 23. This means the iOS 27.1 codebase contains extensive references to the iPhone Duo, which Apple wants to keep under wraps before the product officially goes on sale. As a result, iOS 27.1 will be exclusive to the iPhone Duo.

The software versions for the iPhone Duo and other iPhone models will eventually merge — possibly through an iOS 27.2.x update, or potentially iOS 27.3.

So things will be a bit awkward in the short term, but everything will eventually return to normal.

iOS 27.2 new features

Redesigned Health app

At the iPhone 18 Pro launch event, Apple showed off a brand-new version of the Health app, saying it would arrive later this year. This new app has now surfaced in iOS 27.2 beta testing.

The redesigned Health app is divided into three tabs: Insights, Longevity, and Browse. The app features a completely new design that dynamically adjusts based on your data, and it incorporates Apple Intelligence. The Longevity tab adds a new "Health age" feature that uses Apple Watch data to show how your various metrics compare to your actual age.

The new Health app likely won't launch alongside iOS 27.2 next month. Apple is only just beginning beta testing of the new app, with a full rollout to all users expected later this year.

Further reading: iOS 27.2 brings a major overhaul to the Apple Health app — here's a look at the new features

TV app gains profiles feature

The Apple TV app in iOS 27.2 gets profiles support for the first time. This feature has been available on tvOS for years, but it's making its debut on iPhone.

Further reading: iOS 27.2 brings new profiles feature to Apple TV on iPhone

More Siri AI languages

Siri AI is a headline new feature in iOS 27, and iOS 27.2 extends this capability to more users. Newly supported languages include:

  • French
  • Japanese
  • Korean
  • Portuguese
  • Spanish

Group FaceTime gets Dual Capture mode

In iOS 27, Apple introduced a new Dual Capture feature for FaceTime, allowing you to use the front and rear cameras simultaneously. The person on the other end sees both you and what's in front of you. iOS 27.2 extends this feature to group FaceTime calls for the first time.

Dual Capture requires an iPhone 17 or later, and all participants in the call must be running iOS 27.

Further reading: iOS 27.2 takes FaceTime's best new feature to the next level

Other minor updates

  • In Apple Podcasts, the "Up Next" queue has been renamed to "New Episodes." The "Continue Playing" section now sits directly below New Episodes. The episode list also now uses color-matched backgrounds based on each podcast's cover artwork.
  • In the Music app, some red icons and color accents have been changed to black.
  • iOS 27's Call Context feature, which displays relevant information on screen when you call a business, is now being expanded to include anniversary information.
  • The Clock app's alarm interface has some minor changes, such as smaller font sizes for the AM and PM labels.

Hints at more features to come

Finally, the iOS 27.2 codebase also reveals several other potential upcoming features for iPhone, including a new album release countdown in Apple Music, third-party app support for Describe a Shortcut, and new themes for CarPlay Ultra. iOS 27.2 also shows Apple continuing to work on iPhone anti-theft features.

These features aren't live in iOS 27.2 yet, but the code shows Apple is actively developing them.

iOS 27.2 release date

iOS 27.2 is expected to officially roll out to iPhone users sometime in October. Apple has promised that Siri AI will gain more languages in October, and iOS 27.2 is precisely the update adding these new languages — so the update must ship before November for Apple to deliver on that promise.

Wrap-up

Are you trying out the iOS 27.2 beta? Have you found any useful new features? What do you think of the new Health app? Share your thoughts in the comments.
